sections.h2: Which Jackson offices deal with Butts County property tax?
sections.html:
Value and billing live in two different suites of the same building at 625 W. 3rd Street. Suite 1 is the Board of Tax Assessors, which decides what your house is worth. Suite 2 is the Tax Commissioner, an elected office that mails the bill and takes the payment.

The county's own pages stress that these are separate jobs, and that the tax commissioner answers to voters and the state revenue department rather than to the assessors or the commissioners. For a seller, that means a question about a number on a valuation notice and a question about a payoff go to different counters.

  • Assessors: 770-775-8207, weekdays from 8:00 to 4:30.
  • Tax Commissioner: 770-775-8206, weekdays from 8:00 to 4:00, closed on approved holidays.
  • Clerk of Superior Court: holds recorded deeds and liens, and can give you a copy of your warranty deed.

The assessors' general information page says the tax is figured on 40 percent of fair market value as fixed each January 1. The county government and the school board then set their own mill rates, and a mill is $1.00 per $1,000 of assessed value.

sections.h2: What are the Butts County tax installments?
sections.html:
Butts County bills real estate and personal property in two parts: September 15 and December 7. A date that falls on a weekend slides to the following business day. Mobile and manufactured homes are on a separate April 1 date.

Statements go out to the owner, never to a mortgage servicer. The office does send servicers a data file, yet if your lender pays from escrow you may still need to hand over a paper copy. A buyer who closes mid-year will see the bill in their own name, and the office asks you to call if a statement shows up for a house you already sold.

Part payments are welcome and you may make several, but interest and penalties continue to build on the unpaid part, and an account with any balance can be liened. The FAQ gives two different answers on mailed payments, one saying the postmark is not honored and one saying a USPS postmark is. Settle that with the office before you drop a check in the mail.

sections.h2: What did the 2026 countywide reappraisal change in Butts County?
sections.html:
Butts County hired Georgia Mass Appraisal Solutions to review about 13,000 parcels for 2026, with field crews starting in July 2025. Appraisers measured buildings and took photos from outside, and the assessors say none of them go inside a home.

The new values are as of January 1, 2026, and the annual notices were mailed in April and May 2026. Then on July 8, 2026, the Board of Assessors posted that appeals had passed 3% of total value, which under Code Section 48-5-311(e)(3)(B) gives the board an additional 180 days to answer 2026 appeals.

If you plan to list a house, look up your parcel on the assessors' search page before choosing an asking price, and ask whether an appeal on it is still open. A value that changes late in the process changes the number the tax commissioner bills.

sections.h2: Where does a Butts County assessment appeal start?
sections.html:
It starts with a written appeal on form PT-311-A, filed with the Board of Assessors within 45 days of the date the notice was sent. Say which method you want. The grounds the commissioner's FAQ lists are taxability, value, uniformity and denial of an exemption.

The assessors review your evidence first, and the county's explainer says they can change the value if they find a mistake. Your next step is the Board of Equalization, a panel of residents appointed by the Grand Jury, or arbitration if you chose that when you filed.

  • Useful proof: a recent appraisal, comparable sales, or photos of defects.
  • A complaint that the bill is too high is outside the grounds, because the appeal is about value and taxability.
  • The forms page says the board cannot waive a late filing or forgive a penalty.

sections.h2: Which Butts County exemption dates matter when you buy or sell?
sections.html:
The homestead application has an April 1 deadline, and the assessors' forms page lists a second form for owners 62 and older showing $20,000 off county tax and $15,000 off school tax. You must own and live in the house on January 1. A move, or a new name on the deed, means applying again.

Returns for real and personal property are taken at the assessors' office from January 1 to April 1. Farm use valuation on form PT-283A has the same April 1 cutoff, and the office wants a phone call before you submit it.

A relief that belongs to the seller does not follow the house. Whoever buys and plans to live there files their own application ahead of the following April 1.

sections.h2: How does a lien form on a Butts County house?
sections.html:
Before any lien, the tax commissioner sends a 30-day notice of intent. Tax still open more than 90 days after its due date can then be recorded as a FiFa on the General Execution Docket at the Clerk of Superior Court. Paying the tax plus the fees, interest and penalties cancels it.

Liens are not sold over the counter in Butts County. Where a levy and tax sale advertisement has started, the FAQ urges paying in person. A recorded FiFa is public and can reach your credit file, and the office says it does not report to the bureaus.

A title company will not close over an open lien. Request a written payoff with a good-through date from the tax commissioner and hand it to whoever runs the settlement.

sections.h2: What kind of place is Butts County to sell in?
sections.html:
Butts is a West Central Georgia county of 184 square miles of land, created on December 24, 1825 as the 64th county from parts of Henry and Monroe. Jackson is both seat and largest city. Flovilla and Jenkinsburg are the other incorporated cities, and Stark and Worthville are unincorporated communities. Interstate 75, U.S. 23 and State Routes 16, 36, 42 and 87 cross it.

Atlanta's metro area includes the county, which touches Henry, Spalding, Lamar, Monroe, Jasper and Newton counties. Jackson Lake took shape in 1910 behind the Lloyd Shoals dam on the Ocmulgee River, and Indian Springs State Park is the oldest state park in the nation, according to the assessors' own site. The county's courthouse of 1898 was used until 2019 and is now a museum and visitor center.

faqs.q: Can a Butts County house with back taxes still be sold?
faqs.a: Yes. The unpaid tax, interest and penalties come out of the proceeds at closing and the lien is released. Get a payoff with a good-through date from the tax commissioner at 770-775-8206, since the amount rises as the months pass.

faqs.q: Which Butts County office answers a bill question?
faqs.a: The Tax Commissioner at 770-775-8206 answers bill, payoff and lien questions. The Board of Assessors at 770-775-8207 answers value, exemption and appeal questions. Both are at 625 W. 3rd Street in Jackson.

faqs.q: Does my lender receive the Butts County bill?
faqs.a: No, the statement goes to the owner. The office sends mortgage companies on record a data file, so a lender that escrows may already know the amount. If you have changed lenders, tell the new one and forward the bill yourself.

faqs.q: When must I apply for homestead in Butts County?
faqs.a: By April 1. That deadline is listed for the standard exemption and for the one for owners 62 and older. A form that arrives after April 1 takes effect in the following tax year.

faqs.q: How long is the Butts County appeal window?
faqs.a: Forty-five days from the date the assessment notice was sent. The appeal must be in writing and filed with the Board of Assessors, and the board cannot extend the period.
